title: Reading Drill — Testing a leaflet about river access — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing a leaflet about river access — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The river access officer had been asked to investigate people following a path shown as open when its gate is closed in Hillswick. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on outdated route reports, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a six-week comparison, the team used visitor messages at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because unusual rainfall might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a seasonal route note. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
